keyFindings.text: **Q4 depth — v4.0.2.0 is a tagged release, so the open-release extension path is closed and the amendment path is correction-scoped.** `git tag --list 'v4.0.2*'` returns `v4.0.2.0`. The changelog skill extends only the latest entry that has no release tag on origin and treats in-place extension as the one exception to the no-existing-file rule, while a published entry may be amended with `build_release_notes.py` plus `gh release edit` with the tag left in place; the amendment path is stated for "a correction or a reordering". v4.0.2.0 has that precedent ("The v4.0.2.0 notes were amended four times"). The decisive fact is ancestry: if the ten commits are ancestors of tag v4.0.2.0, amend the entry as a correction; if they are not, the tag bars extension and the default is a new, strictly greater version file. I did not run the ancestry check inside the tool budget; the exact command is `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> v4.0.2.0` for each of the ten.
